t.1.4.1: The blessed sage Vālmīki, master of himself, composed the entire story, rich in varied words, of Rāma, who had regained his kingdom.
t.1.4.2: Having composed it, together with what was yet to come and the sequel, the greatly wise master pondered: "Who now might perform this?"
t.1.4.3: While that great seer of purified soul was pondering, Kuśa and Lava, clad in the garb of hermits, then clasped his feet.
t.1.4.4: Kuśa and Lava, the two glorious princes who knew dharma, were there; he saw those brothers, endowed with melodious voices, dwelling in the hermitage.
t.1.4.5: Seeing those two intelligent youths thoroughly grounded in the Vedas, the master had them learn it by heart, for the purpose of amplifying the Vedas.
t.1.4.7: It was sweet both in recitation and in song, endowed with the three measures of tempo, furnished with the seven musical modes, and accompanied by the rhythm of stringed instruments.
t.1.4.6: He who had kept his vows composed the entire poem, the Rāmāyaṇa, the great story of Sītā, known also as the Slaying of Paulastya.
t.1.4.8: The two sang this poem, endowed with the rasas of humor, love, compassion, fury, heroism, terror, disgust and the rest.
t.1.4.9: Those two brothers knew the true essence of the Gāndharva art of music, were skilled in its registers and modulations, and were gifted with fine voices, like two Gandharvas in bodily form.
t.1.4.10: Endowed with beauty and auspicious marks and speaking with sweet voices, the two were like two images drawn from an original image, two others born, as it were, from the body of Rāma.
t.1.4.11: Those two blameless princes, having made that whole excellent and righteous narrative, the poem, entirely subject to their speech, committing all of it to memory in its fullness...
t.1.4.12: In the assembly of seers, of the twice-born and of the virtuous, those two, knowers of the truth and composed in mind, sang it just as they had been taught: high-souled and most fortunate, marked with every auspicious sign.
t.1.4.13: Once, standing near the assembled sages of purified souls as they sat together, those two sang this poem.
t.1.4.15: All those sages, devoted to dharma and delighted in heart, praised the two singing bards, Kuśa and Lava, who were worthy of praise.
t.1.4.14: Hearing that, all the sages, their eyes brimming with tears, were filled with the greatest wonder, and the two said, “Excellent, excellent!”
t.1.4.16: Ah, the sweetness of the song, and especially of the verses! Though these events took place long ago, they have been shown to us as if before our very eyes.
t.1.4.18: Being thus praised by the great sages, who were renowned for their austerities, the two of them sang still more feelingly, exceedingly sweetly.
t.1.4.17: Then the two of them, having entered fully into it, sang together its feeling beautifully, sweet, moving, and rich in the excellence of their voices.
t.1.4.19: One sage, standing there, well pleased, gave the two of them a water-pot; another, of great renown, gladdened, gave the two of them a garment of bark.
t.1.4.21: Once, Bharata's elder brother saw there, in the streets and on the royal highways, the two singers who were being praised everywhere.
t.1.4.20: Wondrous is this tale proclaimed by the sage, the supreme foundation for poets, and it has been brought to completion in its proper order.
t.1.4.22: Then Rāma, the destroyer of enemies, brought the two brothers Kuśa and Lava into his own house and honored them, who were worthy of honor.
t.1.4.23: And that lord, the scorcher of foes, was seated upon a celestial golden lion-throne, with his ministers and brothers seated close beside him.
t.1.4.24: Then, having seen those two lute-bearers, both endowed with beauty, Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, and likewise to Śatrughna and Bharata.
t.1.4.25: Let this tale, rich in wondrous meanings and words, be heard as these two of godlike splendor sing it well in a sweet voice.
t.1.4.27: Then the two, urged on by Rāma's words, sang with all the excellence of the mārga style. And Rāma too, seated amid the assembly, slowly became wholly absorbed in mind, eager to partake of it.
t.1.4.26: These two sages, Kuśa and Lava, great ascetics endowed with the marks of kings, recite a tale of great majesty which, they declare, brings prosperity even to me; listen to it.
